exec: FAA has paused its router replacement after the ground stop; the DNI said it was not seen as a cyber attack.
impact: More than 9,100 flights were canceled, according to FlightAware as cited by Fox Weather; about 3,500 flights were in the air at the time.
plain: A faulty router installed during maintenance began flooding other routers and air traffic systems on November 13, grounding US flights. The FAA has paused installing those routers and gone back to its old ones.

key_findings: AP: the FAA paused installing the routers linked to the stop and turned off Juniper routers already installed, relying on older Cisco routers.
AP: the problem hit 17 of the nation's 22 regional air traffic control centers; it was linked to a router just installed in El Dorado, Arkansas.
Fox Weather: more than 9,100 flights canceled and more than 24,500 delayed Friday per FlightAware; stop lifted at 8:15 p.m. Friday.
Reuters: DNI Jay Clayton said officials were not seeing this as a cyber attack incident.
report.publisher: Associated Press via BNN Bloomberg (CTV live blog)
recommendations: The FAA paused further installation of the routers and switched off installed Juniper units (AP).

sources.name: BNN Bloomberg / CTV News live updates (AP)

summary: A router installed during maintenance at a remote FAA site began flooding other routers and air traffic systems on November 13, per Secretary Duffy (Fox Weather). AP reports 17 of 22 regional centers were hit; the FAA paused new router installs and switched off installed Juniper units. Fox Weather says the stop lifted at 8:15 p.m. Friday. DNI Clayton said it was not seen as a cyber attack (Reuters).
title: FAA grounds all US departures after air traffic communications failure

validation.note: Review: compared summary with Fox Weather (9,100 cancellations, 3,500 in the air, lifted 8:15 p.m., Duffy: router flooding), BNN/AP (17 of 22, Juniper off, Cisco) and Reuters (DNI Clayton). FAA Q&A page 403, so its figures (12,462, 9,082, 1,000 attempts, FTI network, 60 other routers) were removed from the record.

review.note: Cause, 17 of 22, Juniper/Cisco, 9,100 cancellations, 8:15 pm lift, DNI statement checked against AP/BNN, Fox Weather; FAA page 403 so unverified figures (12,462, 9,082, 1,000 attempts, FTI, 60 routers) removed from summary and report; summary now attributes cause and no-cyber statement
